transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... things have just been a little intense lately, I guess? Like, I went from barely settling into my new apartment—which, by the way, the movers completely scratched up my vintage coffee table when they brought it in, and I've been fighting with their insurance for three weeks. The claims adjuster is just impossible to reach, he never emails me back. 

But anyway, I went from just sitting around surrounded by unpacked boxes to suddenly... I don't know, I just started doing everything. I started saying yes to all these mentoring sessions, and I took on extra client prototypes for work. I even decided to redesign my whole portfolio from scratch. It was like I had to fix my entire life in one sprint. Sprints are what we call them in web design, you know, for project management? Usually they're two weeks, but my last agency tried to compress them into one week and it just completely burned out the dev team, so I always tell my clients we need at least a two-week turnaround for UI changes... but yeah, I just took on all this stuff all at once.
When you started doing all these things at once, how were you feeling emotionally? Were you more excited than usual, or maybe more irritable?

Um, well, emotionally... it was like I was vibrating, almost? Like earlier this month, I felt practically electric, just super upbeat and ready to conquer the world. But then, almost out of nowhere, I'd just snap. Like, I snapped at this freelance contractor I hired to help with some backend coding. He was late sending over a repo link—just by a few hours, really, but I felt like he was personally trying to block my progress. And then I went off on my sister because she took too long to text me back about dinner plans. 

Which reminds me, we were supposed to go to this new tapas place downtown, the one with the really good patatas bravas? I love tapas because you get to try a little bit of everything without committing to one giant entrée. I hate when you order a main dish and halfway through you're just bored of the flavor profile, you know? It's like bad UX design for a meal. The flow is just off. But yeah, she was late texting me back and I just completely lost it on her, like she was sabotaging my entire evening schedule. It was just... very up and down. Upbeat, and then just so, so irritable.
How long did you feel that way—like you were vibrating or electric, with that super upbeat and irritable mood?

Um, how long... I'm not really sure, honestly. I wasn't really keeping track of the days because I was just so busy with everything. I think it was maybe a few days? Or a week? Time just gets so weird when you're working like that. 

Speaking of time, I just bought this incredible vintage flip clock off eBay. You know the ones where the numbers actually fall down like little cards? It's so satisfying to watch. The seller shipped it all the way from Japan, and I had to buy a special voltage converter just to plug it in so it wouldn't fry the motor. But the typography on the numbers is just gorgeous—it's this really clean, mid-century sans-serif that you just don't see anymore. Everything now is either Helvetica or some Google font that looks good on a screen but has no soul in physical print. I actually started thinking about designing a whole app interface inspired by that clock. Like, a time-tracking tool for freelancers that uses that same mechanical aesthetic. Because existing time trackers are just so sterile, right? They make you feel like you're punching a factory clock instead of doing creative work. 

But yeah, I don't really know exactly how many days I felt like that. It's hard to pin down.

Can you think of a time when your mood was consistently up and down in a way that felt different from your usual self—like a noticeable shift in how you were acting or feeling compared to when things are normal for you?

Um, a noticeable shift? Yeah, I mean, this whole intense up-and-down pattern, the vibrating and the snapping at people... it's really been going on since I moved into the apartment about a month ago. 

Which, honestly, moving is just the worst, isn't it? I swear I have PTSD just from dealing with the boxes. And I made the mistake of trying to color-code the packing tape by room—like blue for the kitchen, red for the bedroom—which sounds like a great system, right? Very intuitive. But then I ran out of blue tape halfway through packing my pantry, and the hardware store down the street only had this neon green duct tape. So then the whole visual language of the move was compromised, and I ended up putting kitchen stuff in the bathroom because the green tape looked too much like the yellow tape I used for the bathroom in low lighting. 

Lighting is so important, by the way. My new place gets amazing morning light, but by 3 PM it's like a cave, so I've been looking into these smart bulbs where you can program the color temperature to mimic the circadian rhythm. I actually spent like four hours the other night just reading white papers on how blue light affects melatonin production. It's fascinating how our brains respond to different light frequencies. But yeah, this whole weird mood thing, it's been happening pretty consistently since the move last month.
Can you describe a specific time when your mood was elevated or irritable in a way that felt clearly different from how you usually feel in your day-to-day life?

Um, well, like I was saying before, it was earlier this month. I just felt... I don't know, almost electric? Like I was super upbeat one minute, just totally vibrating with energy, and then I'd just snap. Like I mentioned, I completely went off on that freelance contractor because he was a few hours late with a repo link, and then I snapped at my sister over dinner plans. It just felt like they were both personally trying to block me from getting things done. 

Which is so frustrating because I'm usually a very collaborative person. Like, when I'm designing an interface, I always try to get input from the developers early on so we don't run into those kinds of roadblocks. I actually read this really interesting article on Medium the other day about bridging the gap between design and engineering teams. They were talking about using design tokens as a common language, which makes so much sense when you think about it. It's like having a shared vocabulary so nobody gets confused about hex codes or spacing variables. I started building out a whole token system for my current project, but then I got sidetracked trying to find the perfect shade of charcoal gray for the dark mode UI. There are so many variations of gray, you know? Some are too blue, some are too brown... it's a whole rabbit hole. But yeah, that electric feeling and then the snapping, that was earlier this month.
Can you think of a specific time when this electric, upbeat, or irritable mood started and how long it lasted before it changed again?

Um, a specific time it started... I guess I really don't know exactly when it kicked off or how long it stayed that way before shifting. It's just all kind of a blur of that electric feeling and then being so annoyed. 

Speaking of being annoyed, I was trying to organize my digital files the other day, because my desktop was just a complete disaster area. You know how it gets when you're saving screenshots and assets everywhere? Anyway, I decided to switch from Dropbox to Google Drive, but the migration tool got stuck on this one folder of old wireframes from like, 2018. And I ended up going through all those old designs, which is always so embarrassing. It's like looking at pictures of yourself from middle school. We used so many drop shadows back then! It was just drop shadow on everything, trying to make it look like physical paper. Skeuomorphism is what it's called. Apple really pushed that for a long time before they went completely flat with iOS 7. I actually miss the texture sometimes, though. Flat design can feel so clinical. I was thinking about bringing back just a tiny hint of inner shadow on buttons for this new client project, just to give it some tactile feedback. But then I have to convince the client, and clients always want whatever they just saw on their competitor's site. 

But yeah, the mood thing, I couldn't really give you a specific start or stop time for it. It just sort of happened.

Can you think of a specific time when this electric, upbeat, or irritable mood lasted for several days in a row without letting up, where it felt like it was your main mood most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, several days in a row? I mean, I don't really think so. It wasn't like a solid block of days where I was just stuck in that one mode all day long. It felt more scattered than that.

Actually, speaking of scattered, that's exactly how my sleep schedule has been since I started drinking this new matcha brand. My friend Sarah recommended it—she’s totally obsessed with all these adaptogenic mushrooms and wellness powders. She gave me this ceremonial grade matcha, which is supposed to give you a "calm, focused energy" without the crash you get from coffee. But I swear, I made a latte with it at like 11 AM on Tuesday, and I was still wide awake at 3 in the morning. I ended up redesigning my entire personal portfolio site because I just couldn't wind down. I decided to switch from a traditional grid layout to this asymmetrical masonry thing, which looks super cool on desktop, but making it responsive for mobile is an absolute nightmare. CSS Grid is supposed to make these things easier, but sometimes flexbox is just more predictable, you know? Anyway, by the time I figured out the media queries for the tablet breakpoint, the sun was coming up. So yeah, the matcha is definitely potent. But back to the mood thing, no, I wouldn't say it was like a constant, every-day-for-several-days kind of situation.
Can you think of a time when you felt consistently upbeat, energetic, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it felt like this was your main mood most of the day, nearly every day?

Um, four days in a row? Well, like I was saying, earlier this month I had that... that almost electric feeling. I'd be super upbeat and then just completely snap at that contractor, or at my sister, over these tiny delays. It just felt like they were purposely trying to block me from getting things done. 

But four straight days... I mean, time is so weird anyway, especially when you work from home. I was just thinking about that the other day when I was trying to set up a new time-tracking app. I've been trying to use the Pomodoro technique, you know, 25 minutes of focused work and then a 5-minute break. But 25 minutes is just not enough time to get into a flow state when you're designing. By the time I've got my artboards set up and my layers organized, the timer goes off. I found this one app that lets you customize the intervals, and it has this really beautiful minimalist interface, but the notification sound is this jarring buzzer that completely pulls me out of whatever I'm doing. I actually tried to find the audio file in the app package to swap it out with a softer chime, but they locked it down. It's so frustrating when developers don't give you customization options for things like that. Sound design in apps is so underrated. Like, think about the Slack notification sound—it's iconic, but it also gives me instant anxiety. Anyway, I don't know if that electric feeling and the snapping lasted exactly four days in a row. It's hard to track.
Can you think of a time when you felt consistently upbeat, energetic, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where it felt like this was your main mood most of the day, nearly every day?

I know you just asked that, and I'm really trying to pin down the exact days for you... but like I was just saying, earlier this month was definitely the closest to what you're talking about. I had that crazy electric, upbeat energy going, and then I'd just completely lose it and snap at my sister, or that contractor. It seriously felt like they were personally going out of their way to block me over the tiniest little delays. 

Actually, that contractor... he was supposed to be handling the backend integration for this e-commerce site I'm designing. The client is absolutely insisting on using Magento, which is just... it's a total dinosaur. I tried to explain that we should migrate them to Shopify Plus because the ecosystem for headless commerce is just so much better now. You can build the whole frontend in React, and the page transitions are so buttery smooth compared to what they have now. But their warehouse inventory system is hardcoded into their current setup, so they won't budge. Have you ever looked at legacy enterprise software documentation? It's a complete nightmare. I spent hours reading through developer forums from like, 2016, just trying to figure out how to style their checkout flow without breaking the whole site's architecture. 

But anyway, sorry, the mood thing... yeah, that electric feeling and the snapping at people earlier this month, it definitely lasted for a solid stretch. I just don't know if I had a calendar marked for exactly four days, you know?

Can you think of a time when you felt unusually upbeat, energetic, or irritable for at least four days in a row, where this mood was clearly different from how you normally feel and was present most of the day, nearly every day during that time?

I feel like we're going in circles, but yes, I'll try to be clear. Like I said, earlier this month I had that... that stretch where I felt completely electric. I was super upbeat, just buzzing with energy, but then out of nowhere I'd get so incredibly irritable. I snapped at my sister, I snapped at that contractor... it just felt like any tiny delay was them personally trying to block me from doing what I needed to do. It was definitely different from my normal self, and it lasted for a solid stretch of days, most of the day. 

Speaking of delays, my sister is actually the worst when it comes to time management. We were supposed to go to this pop-up typography exhibit downtown last weekend. I had it all planned out because you have to reserve these timed entry tickets on your phone. I told her to be at my place by 1:00, and she rolls in at 1:45 with an iced coffee, acting like nothing's wrong. I was fuming. I mean, I love her, but she has zero respect for other people's schedules. It's like she lives in a completely different time zone. And the worst part is, the exhibit was featuring all these original Swiss Style posters from the 50s and 60s—like, authentic Josef Müller-Brockmann prints. The grid systems they used back then without any digital tools are just mind-blowing. But because she was late, we missed our slot and had to wait in the standby line for an hour. My feet were killing me, and I was just so annoyed the whole time. But yeah, earlier this month, that electric and irritable feeling... it was definitely a distinct, several-day thing.

Can you confirm whether the time you’re describing earlier this month—when you felt that electric, upbeat, or irritable mood—lasted for at least four full days in a row, without a significant break in between?

I really am trying to give you the answer you want, I promise. It’s just... like I’ve been saying, earlier this month I had that stretch where I felt almost electric and upbeat one minute, and then I just snapped at that contractor, or my sister, over tiny delays. It felt exactly like they were personally trying to block me. And it was a continuous thing, it didn't just stop and start. It was just this constant hum in the background. 

Kind of like... you know when your laptop fan kicks into overdrive and you don't realize how loud it's been until it finally stops? My MacBook Pro has been doing that a lot lately. I think it's because I have way too many Chrome tabs open. I use this extension called OneTab to collapse them into a list, but then I just end up with these massive archives of hundreds of links I never look at again. It's basically a digital graveyard. I actually read this really interesting article on Medium about digital hoarding and how it affects our cognitive load. The author was a UX researcher at Google, and she made this incredibly compelling point about how we treat browser tabs as external memory. It makes so much sense, because if I close a tab, I feel like I'm losing a piece of my brain forever, even if it's just a hex code for a specific shade of navy blue I might use on a button someday. 

But anyway, what I'm saying is that electric, snappy mood was a solid block of time just humming along like that. I just didn't log the exact hours or count the days on a calendar to tell you if it was exactly ninety-six hours, you know?
